A character reference sheet for one original tribal warrior, designed in the spirit of an Australian Aboriginal hunter from a remote desert-and-bush people. Built on the face of the supplied reference person. Neutral studio reference layout showing the same single character across three defined shots for identity locking.
REFERENCE FACE
The character's face is taken directly from the supplied reference photos: adult male, mid-20s to early-30s, warm medium-bronze skin, dark hair with the same curl texture and color as the reference, full dark mustache with a small soul-patch tuft under the lower lip, dark brown eyes, broad straight nose, soft rounded jaw, calm neutral gaze, faint moles on the cheeks. The face, complexion, and facial features must match the reference 100% in every shot.
FACE LOCK
Keep the reference man's face unchanged: same bone structure, same mustache and chin tuft, same eyes, nose, and lips, same complexion and moles. War paint sits on top of this face without changing its features. Do not slim, age, or restyle the face. Keep the reference hair color and curl texture, but the hair is longer than the reference and worn pulled back. Everything else about the face stays identical to the reference.
HAIR AND EARS
Long dark curly hair gathered cleanly into a single bun/knot at the back of the head, pulled back off the face. No loose hair hanging over the face. Both ears are fully exposed, not covered by hair. Ears are pierced, and instead of metal earrings small carved bones are worn through the piercings as primitive ornaments.
CHARACTER DESIGN
An original tribal warrior styled after an Australian Aboriginal bush hunter: weathered desert look, natural earth presence. Hair long and tied back in a single bun, ears exposed with bone piercings. Simple primitive accents only — bone or wood ornaments. No feathered headdress, no ceremonial plumes, no modern items.
PHYSIQUE
Excellent athletic condition: lean, wiry, sinewy build with a dancer's flexibility, not bulky. Low body fat. Clearly defined abdominal muscles and a developed, well-built chest that read plainly. Strong shoulders and forearms, visible muscle separation, taut skin over working muscle. Powerful but supple — a body built for climbing, running, and hunting, not a bodybuilder.
TATTOOS
Extensive tribal tattoos covering chest, stomach, both arms and both legs, mixing heavy blackwork (bold solid black panels and thick bands), dotwork (fine stippled gradients and shaded geometric fields), and rune-style linework drawn from Turkic and Celtic runic motifs — angular Turkic runiform marks combined with interlaced Celtic knotwork and looping rune bands. Roughly 40% of the total body skin is covered in dense solid blackwork, the rest is rune linework and dotwork shading. Both arms are fully sleeved from shoulder to wrist with no bare gaps. A single large centerpiece tattoo dominates the back: a big turtle with a patterned shell filled with rune-knotwork and dotwork, spanning between the shoulder blades down to the lower back. Abstract decorative patterns and runic motifs only, no readable modern letters. Consistent placement and design across all three shots.
WARDROBE AND BODY
Bare torso, fully exposed chest and stomach showing the tattoos. Legs are mostly bare and exposed below the garment. Barefoot, no sandals, bare soles on the ground.
Groin garment is a wrapped-cloth loincloth — NOT fur and NOT tailored shorts. A long strip of fabric wound and folded around the hips and between the legs, wrapping over the groin and the upper thighs so the covered area roughly matches the coverage of short shorts, while clearly reading as hand-wound draped fabric with visible folds, overlaps, and a knotted/tucked closure at the waist — not a sewn garment. The cloth is worn and weathered: frayed edges, loose threads, scattered dirt and dust stains, faded patchy color, and clearly pieced together from several mismatched scraps of fabric of slightly different earth tones and weaves stitched and tucked together. This wrap is the only garment. Modest coverage, nothing explicit.
Face carries war paint: simple horizontal battle stripes across the cheeks and one stripe over the nose bridge, in charcoal-black and ochre-red, slightly smudged like applied by hand — painted over the reference face without hiding its features.
SKIN AND DETAIL
Hyper-realistic skin texture: visible pores, fine surface grain, subtle sheen of sweat on the shoulders and chest, sun-weathered roughness, faint natural tone variation across the body, the reference cheek moles preserved. A few old battle scars present — a pale healed slash across the ribs, a short scar on one forearm, a small mark on the brow — healed and natural, not bloody or fresh. Scars sit slightly raised or paler than surrounding skin. Skin reads as living tissue over real muscle, with natural creases at the joints.
